item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B directly implements the frozen contract with minimal, idiomatic reuse of existing repository machinery. Candidate A adds explicitly forbidden association APIs and bypasses FilesService.Add by duplicating its logic.","reasons":["B adds exactly the requested Upload signature, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and passes the resulting replayable body through FilesService.Add.","Routing through Add preserves existing FilesOption handling, headers, request construction, response decoding, and error semantics in one place.","B's tests cover multipart field/name/content, retry of a non-seekable io.MultiReader, pre-request validation, and propagation of source-reader errors.","A violates scope and the explicit contract by adding six association options, changing FilesOption internals, and introducing NewFileWithFields machinery unrelated to the requested API contract and expressly disallowed by “Do not add association fields.”"],"risks_a":["Upload reimplements Add's request and response path instead of calling Add, creating duplicate behavior that can drift.","The new form-field options change FilesOption behavior and expand the public API beyond the frozen contract.","The helper and changelog changes increase review surface around out-of-scope functionality."],"risks_b":["The retry test validates content only on the second attempt rather than capturing and comparing both complete multipart bodies.","It does not explicitly test FilesOption forwarding through Upload, though the direct call to Add makes that behavior structurally clear and existing Add coverage remains applicable."]}
